coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Pier 70 Hoedown Yard 1/2 (HDY1/2)
record.summary: The southern parcel of the PG&E-owned Hoedown Yard along 22nd Street, drawn as one flexibly zoned parcel 'HDY1/2' in the D4D height figure (65 ft) and shown as commercial in the D4D Mid-Point scenario; like HDY3 it is outside Brookfield's 28-Acre Project and depends on the City exercising its option to buy the yard from PG&E. No sale, developer or construction has been recorded.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. CORRECTED 2026-09-17: fixed a resolution-mismatch bug that had gone unnoticed since 2026-09-16 -- see digitization_method.
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of Brookfield's larger, largely unaddressed 28-acre site), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named parcels -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Residential per Brookfield's leasing brochure, 65 ft max per Figure 6.4.2. Shown as one combined parcel (HDY1/2) distinct from HDY3 in the D4D's own figure -- not three separately-numbered HDY1/HDY2/HDY3 parcels as sometimes described secondhand. No construction-start source found.

facts.value: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (approximately 3.6-acre parcel per the D4D, 'approximately 3-acre' per the DDA terms, including a 0.2-acre unbuilt Michigan Street right-of-way easement); the City has an option to purchase

Flexible: shown as commercial in the D4D Mid-Point and Maximum Office scenarios and residential in the Maximum Residential scenario; Retail and Service frontage for HDY3 and HDY1/2 may be combined on 22nd Street
no more than six residential stories (D4D S6.4.2)

To be subdivided into three separate parcels and offered for sale by the City; the City may ask the Hoedown Yard developer to build Irish Hill Park, paid with special taxes and the Port's share of tax increment (2017 DDA major terms)
In the Pier 70 SUD but not part of the 28-Acre Project or the developer's option
Infrastructure and Revitalization Financing District No. 2 (Hoedown Yard), whose tax increment may fund affordable housing (unlike the Port IFD)
Named for the former PG&E 'Hoedown Yard' (D4D)

costs.what: Estimated annual CFD special taxes from Parcel K North and the Hoedown Yard for maintenance of Irish Hill Park, Michigan Street, Crane Cove Park and other areas north of 20th Street (2017 projection)

open_questions: Whether the City has exercised its option to buy the Hoedown Yard from PG&E, and whether the IRFD was actually formed after the October 24, 2017 hearing: no Port or Board document after 2017 mentioning either was found.
The Port's 2026 phasing exhibit leaves the Hoedown Yard and PKS uncolored (they are not developer parcels), so no phase is recorded here.
Assessor block/lot for the yard is given as 4120/002 and 4711/008A in the 2017 memo but 4120/002 and 4110/008A in the D4D; one is a typo, unresolved.

No basis for an expected-completion date was found: the Hoedown Yard is explicitly treated as a separate transaction outside the 28-Acre Project's DDA Schedule of Performance (Port Commission Item 11A, Aug 3, 2017, p.1) and the Port's 2026 proposed phasing exhibit leaves it uncolored; no Port or Board document after the 2017 resolutions of intent addresses a schedule for the City's still-unexercised PG&E purchase option, so this record stays undated rather than borrow the 28-Acre Project's buildout target.
